"SPRINKLES" Decoded: Film Screening & Discussion

FREE EVENT! Here is the direct link to the tickets: https://bit.ly/4x0r98Y It is also listed on the homepage of www.salemathenaeum.net -------------------------------------------------------------- Join us at Cinema Salem for special screening of the award-winning short film “SPRINKLES” and a post-screening conversation with film director and co-founder of Artist’s Web Productions, Andrew Korzenik. “SPRINKLES” Decoded is an educational experience that explores the intersection of alternative media, conspiracy theories and the rise of extremist violence. The program begins with a screening of the award winning short film “SPRINKLES”: a suspenseful reimagining of a real life event set in a donut shop. Postscreening, Korzenik will lead an interactive, apolitical conversation about the film, the real life forces that inspired it, and how engaged citizens can push back against extremism. Andrew Koreznik, director of Sprinkles, will lead a Q&A after the film. Andrew Korzenik is a filmmaker and writer based in Chicago, Illinois. After a childhood spent in New England, Andrew moved to Chicago where he was introduced to documentary theater and, more broadly, the idea that storytelling could spark real world conversation. His production company, Artist’s Web Productions, is currently working to independently fund and produce a feature film adaptation of SPRINKLES.

Demons 2

Directed by Lamberto Bava. Starring David Edwin Knight, Nancy Brilli, and Coralina Cataldi-Tassoni. Just when you thought it was safe to watch television... Inside a modern high-rise apartment complex, a mysterious horror broadcast unleashes a demonic plague that transforms residents into bloodthirsty monsters. As the infection spreads from floor to floor, the building quickly descends into chaos, trapping survivors in a desperate fight against an army of flesh-ripping demons. Bigger, bloodier, and somehow even more outrageous than the original, DEMONS 2 takes everything fans loved about DEMONS and cranks it to maximum volume with a new wave twist. Joining us for this diabolical presentation is Salem’s own Wretched Lydia who is dying to see the UNCUT VERSION of one of the most gloriously excessive horror films of the 1980s on the big screen. Whether you're a longtime fan or simply curious what happens when an '80s horror sequel decides "more" is the answer to every question, you're in for one hell of a night. Meet Wretched Lydia: a 3036-year-old sorceress with a minor in necromancy, a temporarily deposed empress, and most importantly, Salem's most hated horror hostess! Prepare to be dragged into the dredges of the worst horror has to offer, from schlocky cult classics and questionable spooky narratives to foul live events and beyond. Think of her as your own personal Elvira, but worse. You can find Lydia on all socials @wretchedlydia and live at Koto Salem every third Thursday of the month for a live movie event complete with riffing, chaos, and the illustrious co-host Dick Kayin. See you there, if you dare...

King Lear

We are delighted to host the Cambridge (UK) American Stage Tour’s performance of Shakespeare’s King Lear. This is the third year we've been a stop on the company's annual U.S. tour. The aging King Lear decides to divide his kingdom among his three daughters, allotting each a portion in proportion to the eloquence of her declaration of love. The hypocritical Goneril and Regan make grand pronouncements and are rewarded; Cordelia, the youngest daughter, who truly loves Lear, refuses to make an insincere speech to prove her love and is disinherited. The two older sisters mock Lear and renege on their promise to support him. Cast out, the king slips into madness and wanders about accompanied by his faithful Fool. Cordelia, having married the king of France, is obliged to invade her native country with a French army in order to rescue her neglected father. There will be a 15 minute intermission.

Reset Button Brass Band Presents "Undertale Live"

Back by popular demand, Reset Button Brass Band is excited to present "UNDERTALE LIVE!" on Sunday, September 27 at Cinema Salem! Reset Button will play the music of the Undertale Soundtrack while the video game is played live on the big screen. All songs are arranged and choreographed by Reset Button for this live event. The video game and its original music were created by the amazing and incomparable Toby Fox. Doors open at 3:30pm. Performance is 4-7pm with three short intermissions. Reset Button is a 6-piece brass band with members from Boston's North Shore, specializing in video game music, cartoon theme songs, funky originals, and pop song mashups, including Jamie Green Klopotoski from Gloucester on Baritone Saxophone, Timothy "Timski" Klopotoski from Gloucester on Tuba, Nicholas "Cheeks" Capello from Gloucester on Alto Saxophone, Ian Brown from Nahant on Tenor Saxophone, Ben Tuck from Salem on Trombone, and Ryan French from Salem on Drums.

Sunday 27, September

Rose of Nevada

Three decades ago, the Rose of Nevada vanished at sea, along with its crew. Now, it has returned. In a remote fishing village, its reappearance is embraced as an auspicious sign, with the local citizens convinced the luck of their economically devastated community may turn, if only the ship sails again. Joining the crew is Nick (George MacKay), desperate to provide for his young family, and Liam (Callum Turner), a mysterious drifter eager to escape his past. After a successful voyage, they return to harbour, only to find that nothing is as they remember it. Shooting on a 16mm Bolex camera and constructing all the sound in post, Mark Jenkin writes, directs, edits and scores a haunting and hallucinatory time-travel mystery that further solidifies him as one of the most distinct, singular artists working in film today. Jenkin conducts a cinematic séance, conjuring a portal into another world that forces us to confront the past and our relationship to it.

After the record-breaking global success of Spider-Man: No Way Home, Spider-Man: Brand New Day marks an entirely new chapter for Peter Parker and Spider-Man. Four years have passed since the events of No Way Home, and Peter is now an adult living entirely alone, having voluntarily erased himself from the lives and memories of those he loves. Crime-fighting in a New York that no longer knows his name, he's devoted himself entirely to protecting his city — a full-time Spider-Man — but as the demands on him intensify, the pressure sparks a surprising physical evolution that threatens his existence, even as a strange new pattern of crimes gives rise to one of the most powerful threats he has ever faced.
